role: The Discord surface onto KGSM — a channel per server, live status, and authorized commands from chat.

fields.label: Log level
fields.description: Minimum severity this leaf logs.

fields.label: Bot token
fields.description: Token the bot signs in to Discord with. Without a valid one it cannot connect at all.

fields.label: Guild store
fields.description: The file the bot records each Discord server's setup in — its announcement channel and its per-server channels. Written by /setup in Discord, not here. Losing it loses every channel a server's history is in.

fields.label: Discord application id
fields.description: The Discord application people sign in through on the surfaces that have a sign-in. The bot itself does not, and works without this.

fields.label: Discord application secret
fields.description: Secret for that application. Only the surfaces with a sign-in use it; the bot does not.

fields.label: Account store
fields.description: The file this host keeps its KGSM accounts in, shared with the Control Panel and the assistant. Someone's Discord account decides who they are; the account it is connected to decides what they may do here.

fields.label: Buttons on announcements
fields.description: Whether an announcement about a server that is down carries a button to restart it. Pressing it needs the same permission the command does.

fields.label: Threads for crashes
fields.description: Whether a crash opens a thread under its announcement, so the conversation about it stays with it instead of scrolling the channel. Needs permission to create threads.

fields.label: Server started
fields.description: A server's process was launched.

fields.label: Server ready to play
fields.description: A server finished loading and is playable. Follows every start, including the ones the supervisor makes on its own, so leaving it off keeps a channel to one message per start.

fields.label: Server stopped
fields.description: A server was stopped.

fields.label: Server restarted
fields.description: Someone cycled a server deliberately.

fields.label: Server crashed
fields.description: A server died unexpectedly and the supervisor is restarting it. Announced once per crash, not once per restart attempt.

fields.label: Server gave up restarting
fields.description: The supervisor ran out of restart attempts and left a server down. This is the one that means somebody has to go look.

fields.label: Game update available
fields.description: A newer game build was released for a server. Announced once per build, not once per check, and only for servers this host actually checks.

fields.label: Game updated
fields.description: A new game build was applied to a server.

fields.label: Server installed
fields.description: A new server was installed.

fields.label: Server uninstalled
fields.description: A server was uninstalled.

fields.label: Backup created
fields.description: A backup of a server was written.

fields.label: Backup restored
fields.description: A backup was rolled back onto a server, replacing what was there.

fields.label: Player joined
fields.description: A player connected. One message per join — busy on a popular server.

fields.label: Player left
fields.description: A player disconnected. One message per leave.

fields.label: Player kicked or banned
fields.description: A player was kicked, banned, or had a ban lifted.

fields.label: Delete channel with the server
fields.description: Whether uninstalling a server also deletes its Discord channel, taking that channel's history with it. Off, the channel is left behind.

fields.label: Running marker
fields.description: Shown beside a server that is running.

fields.label: Stopped marker
fields.description: Shown beside a server that is stopped.

fields.label: Uninstalled marker
fields.description: Shown beside a server that is no longer installed.

fields.label: Clean up announcements
fields.description: Whether announcements are deleted again after a while, so a busy channel does not fill with them. On, the channel keeps no record of what happened.

fields.label: Announcement lifetime
fields.description: How long an announcement stays before it is deleted.

fields.label: Status message floor
fields.description: How long the bot waits before editing the live status message again, so a burst of changes becomes one edit instead of one each.

fields.label: Status message refresh
fields.description: How often the live status message is refreshed even when nothing has happened, to catch anything no event reported.

fields.label: Show the host in the member list
fields.description: Whether the bot shows how many servers are up beside its name in the member list. It needs no channel and no setup, and every Discord server sees the same line.

fields.label: Presence refresh
fields.description: How often the bot re-checks the host to update the line beside its name. Set it low and Discord will start refusing the updates.

fields.label: Send floor
fields.description: How long the bot waits between two messages it sends on its own, so a burst is spread out instead of arriving at once and getting the bot throttled.

fields.label: Send queue size
fields.description: How many messages may wait to be sent before the bot starts refusing new ones and saying so. Reaching this means Discord is not keeping up with this host.

fields.label: Send attempts
fields.description: How many times the bot re-tries a message Discord could not take, before giving up on it. Only a temporary failure is re-tried.

fields.label: Backoff
fields.description: How long the bot pauses everything it is sending after Discord refuses a message for a temporary reason. It doubles each time until the ceiling below.

fields.label: Backoff ceiling
fields.description: The longest the bot will pause between re-tries, however many times sending has failed.

fields.label: Public address
fields.description: The address the bot tells people to connect to — a domain name, if this host has one. Left blank, it uses the external IP address the host measures for itself.

fields.label: KGSM executable
fields.description: Path to the KGSM executable. Everything the bot knows about this host's servers is read through it.

fields.label: KGSM event journal
fields.description: Directory holding the engine's event journal, which the bot reads so a channel's status updates the moment a server starts or stops. Read-only and shared with every other consumer — nothing needs configuring on the engine side.

fields.label: Watchdog socket
fields.description: The supervisor's control socket, which the bot starts and stops servers through.

fields.label: Status socket
fields.description: Where the bot publishes its status for the Control Panel to read — gateway state, each Discord server it is set up in, and its channel map. Leave blank to serve no status at all.

fields.label: Firewall socket
fields.description: The firewall authority's control socket, which the bot asks whether a server's ports are actually reachable. It only ever reads.

fields.label: Server list cache
fields.description: How long the list of servers is reused before being re-read from KGSM.

fields.label: Blueprint cache
fields.description: How long the blueprint catalog is reused before being re-read from KGSM.

fields.label: Assistant address
fields.description: Where the assistant service is reached. It is normally on this same machine. Left blank, the bot still runs commands and announces, and only answering questions is unavailable.

fields.label: Assistant relay secret
fields.description: Shared secret the assistant recognises this bot by. It has to match the assistant's own, and without it the assistant refuses every question the bot asks on someone's behalf.

fields.label: Answer timeout
fields.description: How long to wait for an answer before giving up. A question that has the assistant check several servers takes longer than a simple one.
